agenda_items.note: THE main event — 60-minute SED-led discussion. Separate file contains the CEY workbook (26.08.27_NAP_CEY Data_Jerry.xlsx, 39 tabs, 1,309 rows). Full analysis in scratchpad.
flags: 82.3% of the 1,309 CEY rows are yellow (below 95% of their own multi-year average) — Jerry is asking STC to fix

Data-quality suspects: Sugar Beet Yuma (unit anomaly + Woody's RMA-insurable finding), Sorghum Montezuma (single 2027 stub value = 1.0 bu/ac), Onions Red 27.09 (identical value stamped across Otero/Crowley/Fremont — propagation error)

key_facts.summary: SED-led discussion on whether/how to revise NAP County Expected Yields (CEY) that Jerry says have been systematically depressed by using disaster-year production data.
key_facts.matter: Reconsider how CEYs are set across 1,309 rows (63 crops × 65 counties)
key_facts.authority: 1-NAP handbook — CEY should reflect 'average production potential… STC should ensure that the yield information is comparable with previously approved yields and justify any deviations'
key_facts.sed_position: Current CEYs violate the handbook standard; 82.3% of rows are below their own average, some as low as 17% of average
key_facts.moral_hazard_answer: Lincoln County sorghum: 23 bu × $4.61 × 65% = $68.92/ac NAP guarantee — nowhere near break-even. Producers cannot game NAP at those levels
key_facts.middle_path_motion: Direct SED + FPC to (a) reconcile data-quality issues flagged (Sugar Beet Yuma, Sorghum Montezuma, Onions Red statewide, Mixed Forage baselines) and (b) propose a specific CEY methodology (Olympic vs arithmetic, symmetric vs one-way) for STC adoption at October regular meeting
pros_for: 1-NAP handbook language Jerry cites is authentic and Jerry's reading is defensible
82.3% yellow is not a rounding issue — it's systematic depression relative to production potential
Otero/Crowley are among the most-suppressed counties (78.8% and 87.7% yellow respectively) — ties directly to the Item 9a Otero PP question
Producer safety net is measurably reduced by current CEYs — Lincoln sorghum guarantee at $68.92/ac makes the moral-hazard concern implausible
Jerry has spent weeks gathering primary producer data (Pueblo State Fair, Delta, Grand Junction, CSU Extension) — proposal is not underprepared
cons_risks: Options 1 and 3 both touch 87-95% of the entire CEY table — mass revision on a same-morning email creates documentation burden
Option 3 is asymmetric (floor without ceiling) — 'not a formula, a policy'
Jerry's arithmetic mean methodology differs from the 1-NAP-standard 5-year Olympic average — approving Option 1/3 without noting this creates a documentation gap
103 blue rows (≥106% of avg) would be CUT under Option 1 — those may reflect prior STC deviations justified in the record
Data-quality problems (identical-value propagation, unit anomalies, single-year stubs) should be fixed regardless of policy option — voting on those rows as-is bakes in errors

agenda_items.note: STAFF IS ASKING FOR REVERSAL. Doug Andresen's discussion record explicitly requests STC reconsider its Aug prior determinations. This is not a neutral presentation.
flags: 36 Otero/Crowley producers denied Prevent Plant — this is the scope
STC 'acting as the Otero COC' — the actual COC is currently disempowered per March 17 admin action
Both Otero and Crowley WERE in D3+ on every crop's final plant date in 2026 — the D3 test was met
The 2026 denial was under the ineligibility provision (inadequate water beginning BEFORE 3/15 NAP closing), not under the D3 test

2025 vs 2026 goalpost-shift: 2025 producers were told INELIGIBLE because they were NOT in D3+; 2026 same producers told INELIGIBLE because they were on drought monitor for TOO LONG
Gardner Farms Otero: RMA approved PP on Fields 1 & 3, NAP disapproved PP on Field 4 — same producer, same year, adjacent fields

key_facts.summary: Doug Andresen is asking STC (acting as Otero/Crowley COC) to reconsider Aug denials of Prevent Plant claims for 36 producers in Otero and Crowley counties.
key_facts.matter: Review previous Otero/Crowley Prevent Planting determinations
key_facts.authority: 7 CFR 718.103 (prevented planted acreage), 2-CP (Rev. 16) ¶36-37 (PP procedure), 1-NAP ¶51 (NAP causes of loss), 1-NAP ¶300 (NAP application closing dates)
key_facts.sed_position_via_doug: Reverse the 36 denials. Canal-notice-after-3/15 supports reasonable-expectation-of-adequate-water test. RMA/NAP inconsistency is an equity failure. 2025-vs-2026 goalpost shift is not defensible policy administration.
key_facts.reg_reading_that_matters: 2-CP ¶37D lists as ineligible: 'inadequate supply of irrigation water beginning before … the NAP application closing date for the crop.' The operative question is when the water inadequacy started — if canal notices were dated after 3/15, the ineligibility rule doesn't attach.
tracks_available: A. Reverse all 36 denials as Doug recommends — most producer-favorable, matches D3+ facts and the reasonable-expectation reading
B. Reverse subset with carve-out — approve where producer can show canal-company reduction letter dated after 3/15; uphold denials without such documentation. Operationally clean split
C. Uphold + set going-forward standard — keep the Aug denial; adopt a bright-line COC rule for 2027 (e.g., specific water-notice date test). Highest NAD-appeal exposure
pros_for: D3+ threshold test was met on every crop's final plant date in 2026
Canal-company reduction letters after 3/15 support the 'reasonable expectation' test
RMA approved PP on same producer's adjacent fields (Gardner Farms) — inconsistent NAP treatment is an equity failure
Steve Raftopoulos already had doubt on the record at the Aug determination — that doubt is unresolved
36 producers denied is a systemic pattern, not an individual error
Doug is warning that denials will be hard to defend on NAD appeal — reversing now is procedurally cleaner than being reversed by NAD
Ties directly to Item 8 CEY discussion: Otero/Crowley are also the most CEY-suppressed counties. Same pattern of under-service to SE Colorado
cons_risks: Reopening prior STC determinations weakens the finality of committee action generally
If producers already received NAD-appeal-rights notices on current denials, reconsideration restarts the 30-day clock per 7 CFR 780.9 and may complicate active appeals
The Aug 27 delegation moved CCC-576 authority to DDs — clarify procedurally whether STC still holds these 36 or whether they now sit with the DD
Setting a going-forward standard (Track B or C) requires a definitional debate that could consume additional time beyond the 30-min allocation
Reversing all 36 without documenting the reasonable-expectation basis creates its own record vulnerability

meeting_notes.topic: Virtual Fence Collar Costs — Rate-Setting Reference (Items 5a / 6a)
meeting_notes.detail: Two structural cost approaches: (1) BASE-STATION SYSTEMS — Vence ~$40/collar/yr subscription + $10-12.5K base station + $18-24/head/yr data; Gallagher eShepherd $250/collar (3-yr warranty) + ~$5K base station (only where cell weak) + ~$18/collar/yr; Halter bundled collars + ~$4.5K infrastructure + ~$84/head/yr. Best economics at larger herds amortizing base station. (2) CELLULAR / NO BASE STATION — Nofence $289-$345/collar (5-yr warranty), no base station, subscription $54-$78/collar/yr after Yr-1 waiver. Higher collar capex but scales linearly, better for smaller/scattered herds. 200-head first-year ballpark: Vence ~$22K, Halter ~$21K, Gallagher ~$55K, Nofence ~$58K. NRCS EQIP 645 (Fence — Virtual) 2025 CO payment schedule runs ~$100-$150/head — worth cross-checking so CRP/EFRP rate stays aligned with NRCS.
